model.name: Alias / Same-as Mapping
model.purpose: Provide a reusable, format-neutral mixin for asserting that two identifiers denote the same subject across federated authorities, qualified by asserting authority, confidence and validity, and resolvable deterministically both currently and as of any past instant.
model.scope_statement: WM-XCT-036 governs directed and symmetric equivalence assertions between identifier endpoints held by different authorities. It owns the assertion record (endpoints, asserting authority, confidence, validity interval, evidence links), the provenance and lifecycle of those assertions, and the deterministic resolution service that answers 'which identifiers does this identifier stand for, according to whom, at which instant'. It owns historical (as-of) answering with separated event and observation timelines, version pinning of the endpoints an assertion was evaluated against, admission and traversal governance for externally observed redirect and canonical-hint chains, the consequences for its own assertion population when endpoints are merged, split, withdrawn or tombstoned elsewhere, and concurrency, duplication, conflict-containment and quarantine controls over its own records. It does not own the identifiers themselves, the resources they address, the transport that dereferences them, the reasoning that would infer new equivalences, or the merging of the described subjects' data.
in_scope: Equivalence assertions between two identifier endpoints belonging to distinct authorities or namespaces, each carrying an asserting authority and a confidence qualification
Validity intervals and lifecycle states of each assertion (proposed, active, superseded, withdrawn, quarantined) with full retention of superseded decisions
Deterministic resolution answers, including current answers and reconstructed historical answers bound to an explicit as-of instant
Separation of event/validity time from observation and ingestion time on every assertion, observation and answer
Source and target version pinning, including memento-style or version-identifier binding of the endpoint states an assertion was evaluated against
Admission, ordering, hop budgeting, loop detection and classification of externally observed redirect and canonical-hint chains as evidence
Endpoint condition tracking at resolution time: reachable, stale, missing, unresolved, deprecated or tombstoned
Consequences within this model of externally decided endpoint merge, split, withdrawal and reinstatement events, including cluster re-evaluation requests and impact/readiness reporting
Concurrency control over competing proposals: optimistic precondition tokens, idempotency keys, request fingerprints, duplicate and conflict detection
Compensating actions and emergency quarantine of assertions, without deletion of prior decisions or evidence
Provenance of every assertion, observation, answer and containment action, including agent, activity and generation time
out_of_scope: Minting, format, authority delegation and governance of the identifiers themselves, which belong to the parent identifier model WM-XCT-011
Inference or entailment over equivalence assertions (transitive, symmetric or reflexive closure, cluster formation logic), which belongs to a relation-reasoning model
Execution of HTTP or any other transport dereference, including performing redirects; this model ingests observed hop evidence only
Availability, uptime, caching and error handling of the endpoints or of any resolver operated by another party
Authentication, authorization and enforcement of access decisions; this model declares visibility fields only
Merging, survivorship or reconciliation of the described subjects' master data or records
Delivery, subscription, retry and receipting of notifications about change events
Consumer-side audit trails and evidentiary logs of how answers were used downstream
Probabilistic record-linkage or matching algorithm execution that would generate candidate equivalences
Physical deletion and disposition execution, which is owned by the adopting Dimension's retention policy

boundary_notes.distinction: OWL 2 defines SameIndividual and DifferentIndividuals as assertions whose formal consequences are specified in separate semantics documents; WM-XCT-036 records and resolves such assertions with their authority and confidence, but never computes entailed equivalences or closes a cluster.

RFC 9110 assigns redirect following to the user agent and only advises that clients detect cyclical redirections; WM-XCT-036 consumes a hop sequence that some other component observed and governs how that evidence is admitted, bounded and classified.
Identifier syntax, authority, persistence guarantees and namespace governance sit with the parent; this mixin only pairs already-governed identifiers and qualifies the pairing.

ROR records organizational mergers and splits through predecessor/successor relationships while keeping every identifier resolvable; WM-XCT-036 reacts to such an externally decided change by re-evaluating its own assertions and never merges the underlying records.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Retention and disposition policy of the adopting Dimension
boundary_notes.distinction: DataCite states that a registered DOI cannot be deleted and must continue resolving to a tombstone; analogously this model tombstones rather than erases, and hands actual disposition execution to the adopting Dimension's policy.
ResourceSync defines change documents and discovery of capabilities; WM-XCT-036 produces the impact and readiness content, while transport, subscription and receipting belong to the delivery model.

sources.title: RFC 9110: HTTP Semantics
sources.relevance: Normative source for 3xx redirection semantics, permanent versus temporary relocation (301/302/307/308), 300 Multiple Choices ambiguity, 410 Gone, cyclical-redirection detection, and If-Match/ETag/412 optimistic concurrency.

sources.title: RFC 7089: HTTP Framework for Time-Based Access to Resource States -- Memento
sources.relevance: Primary model for as-of access: Accept-Datetime, Memento-Datetime, TimeGate, TimeMap, Original Resource versus Memento, and the statement that best-match selection is server-discretionary and must be consistent.

sources.title: RFC 6596: The Canonical Link Relation
sources.relevance: Defines the canonical link relation as a preference hint over duplicative or superset content, not an assertion of identifier or real-world identity.

sources.title: RFC 8288: Web Linking
sources.relevance: Abstract link model (context, relation type, target, target attributes), the IANA Link Relation Types registry, and the rule that relation types should not be given inferred additional semantics.

sources.title: RFC 3339: Date and Time on the Internet: Timestamps
sources.relevance: Mandatory seconds and explicit UTC offset in timestamps, the distinct meaning of -00:00 for unknown local offset, and leap-second handling.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.relevance: Provenance vocabulary for assertions, observations and answers: Entity/Activity/Agent, wasGeneratedBy, wasAttributedTo, wasDerivedFrom, wasRevisionOf, wasInvalidatedBy, generatedAtTime, invalidatedAtTime, qualifiedAssociation, hadRole.

sources.title: Decentralized Identifier Resolution (DID Resolution) v1
sources.relevance: Closed resolution-status vocabulary (invalidDid, notFound, methodNotSupported, representationNotSupported, invalidOptions), versionTime/versionId resolution options, and deactivated/canonicalId/equivalentId document metadata.

sources.title: Decentralized Identifiers (DIDs) v1.0
sources.relevance: States that an alsoKnownAs assertion does not prove itself, advises independent verification, and treats equivalence as best assumed only when the relation is reciprocated.

sources.title: ResourceSync Framework Specification (ANSI/NISO Z39.99-2017)
sources.organization: National Information Standards Organization (NISO) / Open Archives Initiative
sources.relevance: Change List / Change Dump model with created, updated and deleted change types and the from/until/at/completed datetime attributes; basis for impact enumeration and change notification content.

sources.title: The Idempotency-Key HTTP Header Field (draft-ietf-httpapi-idempotency-key-header-07)
sources.relevance: Idempotency key plus request fingerprint, replay of the previously computed result, conflict when a key is in flight, rejection when a key is reused with a different payload, and key expiry.

sources.title: Tombstone Pages
sources.relevance: A registered DOI cannot be deleted; withdrawn items keep resolving to a tombstone that must state the identifier, the citation and the reason, and the Registered versus Findable states gate discoverability without erasure.

sources.title: Handling Organization Status Changes in ROR
sources.relevance: Active/inactive/withdrawn record statuses, the rule that identifiers are never deleted or reused and must keep resolving, and predecessor/successor relationships representing mergers and splits without requiring bidirectionality.

sources.title: OWL 2 Web Ontology Language Structural Specification and Functional-Style Syntax (Second Edition)
sources.relevance: Defines SameIndividual and DifferentIndividuals as assertions whose formal consequences are specified in the separate Direct and RDF-Based Semantics documents, grounding the boundary between asserting equivalence and reasoning over it.

bundles.name: Historical and As-Of Resolution
bundles.description: Everything needed to answer an alias question deterministically at a stated instant: the two time axes the question is asked on, the endpoint versions the answer was evaluated against, the closed outcome vocabulary, and the observed condition of each endpoint.
bundles.rationale: Memento shows that time-based access requires an explicit requested datetime, an explicit response datetime and a consistent selection rule; DID Resolution shows that a resolution interface needs a closed status vocabulary plus versionTime/versionId options and deactivation metadata; RFC 3339 fixes the timestamp form. Together these force a distinct top-level concern for answering as of a point in time rather than only now.

layers.name: As-Of Frame and Version Binding
layers.description: The temporal frame of a resolution request and the version state of the endpoints it is evaluated against.

findings.name: As-Of Time Basis and Dual Timeline
findings.description: Every resolution request selects on two independent axes: the real-world validity or event time of the assertions being considered, and the observation or ingestion time at which this model came to hold the evidence. A current answer is the degenerate case where both axes are set to 'now'. Recording only one axis makes a historical answer irreproducible, because evidence that arrived late would silently change a past answer.

questions.text: Which event or validity instant and which observation or ingestion instant does this as-of resolution request select on?
answer_data: as-of event instant as an RFC 3339 timestamp with seconds and explicit offset
as-of observation/ingestion instant as an RFC 3339 timestamp with seconds and explicit offset
flag indicating whether either axis defaulted to request time

questions.text: Is the answer a current answer or a reconstructed historical answer, and how is that difference marked on the answer itself?
answer_data: answer mode code: current or historical-reconstruction
reference to the assertion population snapshot used
statement of whether late-arriving evidence was excluded

questions.text: How is a later answer for the same as-of instant distinguished from an earlier one after new evidence arrives?
answer_data: answer identifier and generation activity per PROV-O wasGeneratedBy and generatedAtTime
prior answer identifier that this answer revises (wasRevisionOf)
enumerated evidence items added or invalidated since the prior answer

questions.text: What rule applies when an assertion's validity interval is open-ended or the asserting authority supplied no time-zone offset?
answer_data: open-interval handling rule (treated as valid until superseded or withdrawn)
rule that a missing offset is recorded as -00:00 meaning unknown local offset, never silently as Z
rejection condition for timestamps lacking seconds or an offset

questions.text: How is clock skew between the asserting authority and this model bounded and disclosed on the answer?
answer_data: declared maximum tolerated skew as a duration
skew note or measured offset per source authority
behaviour when an assertion's event time is later than its ingestion time

data_elements.name: As-of event instant
data_elements.description: The validity/event instant the resolution question is asked about.

data_elements.name: As-of observation instant
data_elements.description: The ingestion/observation cut-off; evidence recorded after it is excluded from the answer.

data_elements.name: Answer mode
data_elements.description: Closed code distinguishing a current answer from a reconstructed historical answer.

data_elements.name: Assertion validity interval
data_elements.description: Start and optional end of the interval in which an assertion is claimed to hold.

data_elements.name: Clock skew disclosure
data_elements.description: Declared or measured skew between the asserting authority's clock and this model's clock.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The time basis is not a document but a pair of scalar fields plus a mode code carried on every request, assertion and answer of this model. Materialising it as a separate artifact would create a second place where the authoritative instants live and would invite drift between the artifact and the records it describes; the reproducibility guarantee depends on these values being inline on the very record whose meaning they fix.

findings.name: Source and Target Version Pins
findings.description: An assertion is evaluated against particular states of its two endpoints. Recording which state was seen turns an unfalsifiable claim into a checkable one and lets a historical answer be re-derived. Where the endpoint authority publishes a version identifier or a time-based access mechanism, the pin binds to it; where it does not, the pin degrades explicitly to an observation timestamp plus a payload digest rather than being omitted.

questions.text: Which version identifier of the source endpoint and which of the target endpoint was this assertion evaluated against?
answer_data: source endpoint version identifier or memento reference
target endpoint version identifier or memento reference
observation timestamp for each endpoint state

questions.text: How is a pin expressed when the endpoint authority publishes no version identifier or time-based access mechanism?
answer_data: fallback pin mechanism code (observation-timestamp-and-digest)
digest of the observed endpoint representation
explicit degradation flag so consumers do not treat the pin as authority-issued

questions.text: Which external version or as-of mechanism is bound for each endpoint namespace, and who declares that binding?
answer_data: per-namespace pin mechanism registry entry
mechanism kind (memento datetime negotiation, resolver versionTime, resolver versionId, authority-native revision id)
owning authority of the mechanism declaration

questions.text: How is a pin checked as still dereferenceable before an answer cites it, and what happens if it is not?
answer_data: last successful pin verification timestamp
verification outcome code
answer degradation rule when a pin can no longer be verified

data_elements.name: Source endpoint version pin
data_elements.description: Version identifier, memento reference or degraded digest pin for the source endpoint state.

data_elements.name: Target endpoint version pin
data_elements.description: Version identifier, memento reference or degraded digest pin for the target endpoint state.

data_elements.name: Pin mechanism
data_elements.description: Closed code naming how the pin was obtained.

data_elements.name: Pin verification instant
data_elements.description: Observation instant of the most recent successful verification that the pinned state is still retrievable.

data_elements.name: Pinned representation digest
data_elements.description: Cryptographic digest of the observed endpoint representation, used when no authority version identifier exists.

artifacts.name: Version pin manifest
artifacts.description: Immutable manifest listing, for one assertion or one answer, every endpoint state pin with its mechanism, digest and verification history.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the authoritative master-system identifier of the assertion or answer it pins, extended by a manifest discriminator; where the adopting Dimension holds no master-system identifier, a governed IRI is used, and only failing that a UUID or ULID assigned by the Dimension.

layers.name: Resolution Outcome Determinacy
layers.description: The closed vocabulary of answers this model may emit, including ambiguity and no-answer outcomes, and the observed condition of each endpoint that shaped the outcome.

findings.name: Deterministic Resolution Status and No-Answer Outcomes
findings.description: A resolution answer carries a status drawn from a closed vocabulary. Where more than one endpoint remains admissible the answer returns the candidate set with an ambiguity status; it never silently elects a canonical endpoint. Where nothing is admissible at the requested instant it returns an explicit no-answer status with a reason, never an empty success. The inputs that determined the status are enumerated so the answer can be recomputed.

questions.text: Which closed status vocabulary may an alias resolution answer carry, and who may extend it?
answer_data: enumerated status codes (resolved-single, ambiguous-multiple, no-admissible-assertion, endpoint-unresolved, endpoint-tombstoned, chain-budget-exhausted, chain-loop-detected, quarantined-suppressed, invalid-request)
extension authority and registration rule for Dimension-local codes
mapping notes to external resolver status vocabularies

questions.text: When several candidate endpoints remain admissible, is one selected as canonical or is the ambiguity returned to the caller?
answer_data: rule that the full candidate set is returned with an ambiguity status
per-candidate authority and confidence carried through unaltered
statement that no tie-break or ranking decision is made by this model

questions.text: What is emitted when no assertion is admissible at the requested as-of instant?
answer_data: no-answer status code and machine-readable reason
distinction between never-asserted, not-yet-valid, expired and suppressed
guidance on what the caller must not infer from a no-answer outcome

questions.text: Which inputs must be enumerated on the answer so the same answer can be recomputed later?
answer_data: ordered list of assertion identifiers considered and their disposition
as-of instants on both axes and the pin manifest reference
digest over the ordered determinant input set

questions.text: Which conditions make an answer non-deterministic and therefore invalid to emit?
answer_data: unpinned endpoint state combined with a historical request
unordered candidate set or unstable tie ordering
incomplete evidence ingestion at the stated observation cut-off

data_elements.name: Resolution status
data_elements.description: Closed status code of the answer.

data_elements.name: Candidate endpoint set
data_elements.description: Ordered set of admissible endpoints with the assertion, authority and confidence that admitted each.

data_elements.name: No-answer reason
data_elements.description: Machine-readable reason accompanying a no-answer or suppressed status.

data_elements.name: Determinant input digest
data_elements.description: Digest over the ordered set of inputs that determined the status, enabling replay verification.

artifacts.name: Alias resolution answer record
artifacts.description: Immutable record of one issued answer: request frame, status, candidate set or no-answer reason, pin manifest reference and determinant digest.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the authoritative master-system identifier assigned by the resolution service of record; where none exists, a governed IRI under the adopting Dimension's namespace; only failing both, a Dimension-assigned UUID or ULID. Series position is a separate ordinal attribute and never the identifier.

findings.name: Endpoint Condition: Stale, Missing, Unresolved and Tombstoned
findings.description: An assertion names two endpoints whose condition may have changed since the assertion was made. Registries such as ROR and DataCite keep identifiers resolvable while marking them inactive, withdrawn or tombstoned rather than deleting them, and HTTP distinguishes an absent resource from one deliberately gone. This model records the observed condition of each endpoint with its observation instant and evidence, and uses it to qualify rather than to erase assertions.

questions.text: What condition did each endpoint present at the observation instant, and on what evidence?
answer_data: condition code (reachable, stale, missing, unresolved, deprecated, tombstoned, withdrawn)
observation instant with seconds and offset
reference to the captured observation evidence item

questions.text: How does a deprecated, withdrawn or tombstoned endpoint change the admissibility of assertions naming it?
answer_data: admissibility rule per condition code (admissible, admissible-with-warning, inadmissible)
requirement that the assertion is retained and marked, never deleted
successor or replacement hint carried through without being treated as an equivalence assertion

questions.text: What distinguishes an endpoint that was unreachable from one that is genuinely absent, in the recorded evidence?
answer_data: transport-level outcome captured by the observing component
distinction between a not-found response, a deliberately-gone response and a failure to obtain any response
number of independent observations and their observers

questions.text: For how long may a prior endpoint condition observation be reused before re-observation is required?
answer_data: staleness budget as a duration, per namespace or condition
behaviour when the budget is exceeded during a current-mode answer
exemption rule for historical-mode answers, which must use the contemporaneous observation

data_elements.name: Endpoint condition
data_elements.description: Closed code for the observed condition of one endpoint.

data_elements.name: Condition observation instant
data_elements.description: Instant at which the condition was observed by the reporting component.

data_elements.name: Condition evidence reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the captured evidence supporting the recorded condition.

data_elements.name: Staleness budget
data_elements.description: Maximum age of a condition observation that a current-mode answer may rely on.

data_elements.name: Successor hint
data_elements.description: Replacement or successor endpoint published by the endpoint's own authority, carried as a hint only.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Endpoint condition is a derived qualification held as fields on the assertion and on the answer, pointing outward to evidence that other components captured and to registries that other authorities own. Declaring a local artifact for endpoint state would create a shadow availability register, which is explicitly outside this model's boundary; the authoritative statement of an endpoint's condition always remains with the endpoint's own authority.

bundles.name: Chain Evidence, Change Impact and Contention Control
bundles.description: The operational failure surface of alias mapping: externally observed relocation and canonical-hint chains, the fallout of endpoint merges and splits, and contention between competing or conflicting assertions about the same endpoint pair.
bundles.rationale: RFC 9110 and RFC 6596 supply the relocation and canonical-hint semantics together with the warning that these are transport preferences rather than identity proofs; DID Core states plainly that an alsoKnownAs assertion does not prove itself; ROR and DataCite supply merge, split and tombstone practice; RFC 9110 conditional requests and the IETF idempotency-key work supply the contention controls. These are operating rather than answering concerns and belong in a separate top-level bundle.

layers.name: Relocation and Hint Chain Evidence
layers.description: How externally observed hop sequences and canonical hints are admitted, bounded, classified and weighted as evidence about identifier equivalence.

findings.name: Chain Traversal Budget, Loop Detection and Relocation Class
findings.description: A hop sequence reported to this model is admitted as an ordered, terminating trace under an explicit hop budget. RFC 9110 only advises clients to detect cyclical redirections and notes a historical five-redirect recommendation, so the budget and the loop rule must be declared locally rather than assumed. Each hop is classified as permanent relocation, temporary relocation or non-relocating hint, because only the permanent class is even a candidate for promotion into an equivalence proposal.

questions.text: How is an externally observed hop sequence admitted, ordered and declared terminated?
answer_data: ordered hop list with per-hop observer and observation instant
termination condition code (terminal endpoint reached, budget exhausted, loop detected, observation failed)
identity of the observing component and its capture method

questions.text: What is the maximum hop budget for a chain and what outcome is emitted when it is exhausted?
answer_data: declared maximum hop count and where it is configured
chain-budget-exhausted status on the answer with the partial trace retained
rule that an unbounded chain is never followed and never silently truncated to a success

questions.text: How is a cyclical chain detected, and what is recorded when a loop is found?
answer_data: cycle detection rule over the ordered set of visited endpoints
loop-detected status plus the repeating endpoint and the hop index of repetition
retention of the loop trace as evidence for later diagnosis

questions.text: How is each hop classified as permanent relocation, temporary relocation or a non-relocating hint?
answer_data: per-hop relocation class code
source signal used for the classification (permanent relocation response, temporary relocation response, canonical link relation, other registered link relation)
rule that a temporary relocation never contributes to a permanent equivalence proposal

questions.text: How is a hop observation bound to the as-of frame of an answer that relies on it?
answer_data: per-hop observation instant with seconds and explicit offset
rule that a historical answer may only use hops observed at or before its observation cut-off
re-observation requirement when the chain is older than the staleness budget

data_elements.name: Hop sequence
data_elements.description: Ordered list of observed hops, each with source endpoint, target endpoint, signal type and observation instant.

data_elements.name: Hop budget
data_elements.description: Declared maximum number of hops that may be admitted into one trace.

data_elements.name: Loop detected flag
data_elements.description: Whether a repeated endpoint was found in the ordered trace.

data_elements.name: Relocation class
data_elements.description: Per-hop classification as permanent, temporary or non-relocating hint.

data_elements.name: Chain termination reason
data_elements.description: Closed code stating why traversal of the trace stopped.

artifacts.name: Chain observation trace
artifacts.description: Append-only trace of one observed relocation or hint chain: ordered hops, per-hop class and observation instant, budget, termination reason and observing component.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the authoritative master-system identifier of the observation run that produced it where the observing system of record assigns one; otherwise a governed IRI, and only failing that a Dimension-assigned UUID or ULID. The hop index is an ordinal within the trace, never an identifier.

findings.name: Transport Hints Are Evidence, Not Identity Proof
findings.description: A permanent relocation response, a canonical link relation or a published alsoKnownAs statement is a preference or a claim about where content is served, not a demonstration that two identifiers denote the same real-world subject. RFC 6596 defines canonical as a preferred IRI over duplicative or superset content; RFC 8288 warns against inferring extra semantics from relation types; DID Core states that an alsoKnownAs assertion does not prove itself and advises independent verification and reciprocity. This model therefore captures hints as attributable evidence and requires a separate, authority-backed promotion step before any equivalence assertion exists.

questions.text: What evidential weight may a permanent relocation or canonical link carry towards identifier equivalence?
answer_data: evidence class and declared weight or confidence contribution
explicit statement that transport relocation alone does not establish subject identity
record of which stronger evidence classes are required alongside it

questions.text: What additional confirmation is required before a captured hint becomes a proposed equivalence assertion?
answer_data: reciprocity check outcome where the target publishes a return hint
named asserting authority willing to stand behind the proposal
promotion-eligibility flag and the rule that failed checks leave the hint as evidence only

questions.text: Who observed the hint, from which endpoint and in which representation?
answer_data: observing agent and activity per PROV-O attribution and generation time
context endpoint the hint was published from
digest of the captured hint payload and its media form

questions.text: Which hint relation vocabularies are recognised, and how are unregistered relation types handled?
answer_data: recognised relation types drawn from the IANA Link Relation Types registry
handling rule for unregistered or extension relation types (captured, never auto-promoted)
mapping notes for non-HTTP hint mechanisms such as resolver equivalence metadata

data_elements.name: Hint relation type
data_elements.description: Registered or extension relation type under which the hint was published.

data_elements.name: Hint observer
data_elements.description: Agent that captured the hint, attributable per PROV-O.

data_elements.name: Hint capture instant
data_elements.description: Observation instant at which the hint was captured.

data_elements.name: Hint payload digest
data_elements.description: Digest over the captured hint payload for integrity and duplicate detection.

data_elements.name: Promotion eligibility
data_elements.description: Whether the hint has passed the checks required to become a proposed assertion.

artifacts.name: Captured hint evidence item
artifacts.description: Attributable capture of one published hint: context endpoint, relation type, target, representation digest, observer and capture instant.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the authoritative master-system identifier of the capture in the observing system of record; otherwise a governed IRI naming context endpoint, relation type and capture instant; only failing that a Dimension-assigned UUID or ULID.

layers.name: Endpoint Change Impact and Readiness Reporting
layers.description: How externally decided merges, splits, withdrawals and reinstatements of endpoints propagate into re-evaluation of this model's own assertion population, and how impact and readiness are reported outward.

findings.name: Merge, Split and Withdrawal Consequences with Readiness Reporting
findings.description: When an endpoint authority merges two identifiers, splits one into several, or withdraws one, the decision is theirs; the consequence for every assertion naming that endpoint is this model's. ROR keeps every identifier resolvable and expresses these events as predecessor and successor relationships that need not be bidirectional, which means a merge or split gives a hint about continuity but not an equivalence. This model records the change event, marks the affected assertions for re-evaluation, enumerates impacted downstream references and emits an impact and readiness report plus notification content.

questions.text: Which externally decided endpoint change events are in-scope triggers for cluster re-evaluation?
answer_data: change class vocabulary (merge, split, withdrawal, deactivation, reinstatement, namespace relocation)
reference to the deciding authority's own change record and its effective instant
ingestion instant at which this model learned of the change

questions.text: How are predecessor and successor endpoints recorded without themselves being treated as equivalence assertions?
answer_data: continuity hint fields separate from the assertion store
explicit non-equivalence note where a split produced several successors
requirement for a named asserting authority before any successor becomes an assertion

questions.text: How is a cluster re-evaluation request raised, tracked and closed?
answer_data: re-evaluation request state (raised, in-review, resolved, abandoned) with instants
set of assertions placed under review and their interim admissibility
closure decision reference and the resulting assertion state changes

questions.text: Who decides the endpoint change, who owns the re-evaluation and who consumes the readiness report?
answer_data: deciding authority identifier for the endpoint change
accountable steward for the re-evaluation within the adopting Dimension
named consumer set for the impact and readiness report

questions.text: How are impacted downstream references enumerated and how is the change made discoverable to them?
answer_data: impacted assertion and answer sets with change type per entry (created, updated, deleted)
change list interval boundaries expressed as from and until instants
readiness signal stating whether consumers may migrate yet

data_elements.name: Endpoint change event reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the externally decided change record at the endpoint's own authority.

data_elements.name: Change class
data_elements.description: Closed code for the kind of endpoint change.

data_elements.name: Impacted assertion set
data_elements.description: Enumerated assertions and answers affected by the change, each with a change type.

data_elements.name: Re-evaluation request state
data_elements.description: Lifecycle state of a cluster re-evaluation request raised by this model.

data_elements.name: Migration readiness signal
data_elements.description: Whether downstream consumers may act on the change yet, and under which conditions.

artifacts.name: Change impact and migration readiness report
artifacts.description: Report for one endpoint change event listing impacted assertions and answers, interim admissibility, re-evaluation state and the readiness signal for downstream migration.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the authoritative master-system identifier of the change event in the deciding authority's register combined with this model's report discriminator; otherwise a governed IRI; only failing that a Dimension-assigned UUID or ULID. Edition ordinals are attributes, not identifiers.

artifacts.name: Alias change notice
artifacts.description: Notification content describing created, updated and deleted alias entries within a stated time interval, prepared for downstream consumers; delivery is performed elsewhere.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the authoritative master-system identifier of the publishing service's notice register; otherwise a governed IRI incorporating the interval start instant; only failing that a Dimension-assigned UUID or ULID.

layers.name: Contention, Duplication and Containment
layers.description: Controls that keep a federated assertion store consistent when several parties propose, retry or contradict assertions about the same endpoint pair at the same time.

findings.name: Concurrent Proposals, Idempotency and Duplicate Detection
findings.description: Two proposals about the same endpoint pair may arrive simultaneously, and any one proposal may be retried after an ambiguous failure. Optimistic concurrency with an expected-version precondition rejects a blind overwrite; an idempotency key combined with a request fingerprint distinguishes a retry from a genuinely new proposal and lets the original outcome be replayed. Semantic duplicate detection is separate again, because two textually different payloads can assert the same equivalence.

questions.text: Which precondition token must a proposal carry so that a lost update is rejected rather than applied?
answer_data: expected-version or entity-tag style validator for the targeted assertion
rejection outcome when the validator does not match current state
policy on whether an unconditional proposal is refused outright

questions.text: How is a retried proposal recognised as the same operation rather than accepted as a new one?
answer_data: idempotency key supplied by the proposing client
request fingerprint or digest over the proposal payload
replay behaviour returning the originally computed outcome, success or failure

questions.text: How is a semantically duplicate assertion detected when its payload differs textually from an existing one?
answer_data: normalised endpoint pair key including direction and authority
comparison rule over validity interval and asserting authority
duplicate-of reference recorded on the later proposal instead of a second active assertion

questions.text: What happens when two proposals for the same endpoint pair are in flight at the same moment?
answer_data: conflict outcome for a key already being processed
serialisation or rejection rule for competing endpoint-pair proposals
guidance to the loser on safe retry after re-reading current state

questions.text: How long is an idempotency key honoured, and what prevents its reuse with a different payload?
answer_data: declared key retention window and expiry behaviour
rejection outcome when a stored key is presented with a different fingerprint
scope of key uniqueness (per proposing client, per operation)

data_elements.name: Expected version token
data_elements.description: Validator naming the assertion state the proposer believed current.

data_elements.name: Idempotency key
data_elements.description: Client-generated key allowing a retry to be recognised as the same operation.

data_elements.name: Request fingerprint
data_elements.description: Digest over the proposal payload, paired with the idempotency key to detect key reuse with different content.

data_elements.name: Duplicate-of reference
data_elements.description: Reference from a rejected duplicate proposal to the surviving assertion.

data_elements.name: Concurrency outcome
data_elements.description: Closed code recording how a contended proposal was disposed of.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Concurrency and idempotency data are control fields carried on the proposal and on the resulting assertion state, not documents in their own right. Their whole value lies in being evaluated atomically with the state transition they guard, so materialising them as a separate artifact would introduce a second write that could itself be lost or reordered. The durable output of a contended proposal is the assertion record and the answer record already declared elsewhere in this model.

findings.name: Conflicting Active Assertions, Compensation and Emergency Quarantine
findings.description: Two authorities may hold contradictory active assertions about the same endpoint pair, and a harmful assertion may need to stop influencing answers before its dispute is settled. Following registry practice that identifiers are never deleted and withdrawn items keep resolving to a tombstone that states the reason, containment here suppresses visibility and issues compensating actions while retaining every prior decision and evidence item unchanged.

effect of each state on answer inclusion and on the ambiguity status

minimum evidence or trigger condition required

field placement rule so a suppressed assertion is never silently absent

data_elements.name: Conflict set
data_elements.description: Group of mutually contradictory assertions about the same endpoint pair, with per-member containment state.

data_elements.name: Containment action
data_elements.description: Closed code for the action taken (contest, suppress, quarantine, withdraw, reinstate).

data_elements.name: Compensating action reference

artifacts.name: Containment and compensation record
artifacts.description: Record of one containment action: conflict set, action taken, raising agent and instant, evidence threshold met, expiry, compensating linkage and the tombstone statement shown in place of the suppressed assertion.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the authoritative master-system identifier of the governing case or decision in the steward's system of record; otherwise a governed IRI under the adopting Dimension's namespace; only failing that a Dimension-assigned UUID or ULID.

functions.name: Resolve alias set as of a stated frame
functions.description: Return the admissible equivalence assertions for a given identifier at a stated event instant and observation cut-off, with a status drawn from the closed vocabulary and never a silently elected canonical endpoint.
inputs: as-of event instant (RFC 3339, seconds, explicit offset)
optional version pin or memento reference per endpoint
outputs: resolution answer record with status, candidate set or no-answer reason
determinant input digest and pin manifest reference
per-candidate asserting authority and confidence carried through unchanged
preconditions: both as-of instants are well formed and the observation cut-off is not earlier than the assertion population's earliest ingestion instant
every candidate assertion has a recorded validity interval and asserting authority
effects: records the answer's provenance activity and generation instant
emits ambiguity or no-answer status rather than selecting a single endpoint

functions.name: Evaluate an observed chain within budget
functions.description: Admit an externally observed hop sequence, order it, detect cycles, apply the hop budget and classify each hop as permanent relocation, temporary relocation or non-relocating hint. This function evaluates evidence; it never performs a dereference or follows a hop itself.
inputs: ordered hop observations with observer, signal type and observation instant
outputs: chain observation trace with termination reason
per-hop relocation class
chain-derived status contribution (loop detected, budget exhausted, terminal reached)
preconditions: each hop carries an observation instant at or before the cut-off
the observing agent is identified and attributable
effects: persists the trace as evidence, including partial and looping traces
never promotes a hop to an assertion by itself

functions.name: Capture a published equivalence hint as evidence
functions.description: Record a published canonical link, relocation response or alsoKnownAs-style statement as attributable evidence, run the reciprocity and authority checks, and set promotion eligibility without creating an assertion.
inputs: context endpoint and published relation type
outputs: captured hint evidence item with payload digest
promotion eligibility flag and the checks that produced it
reciprocity finding where a return hint exists
preconditions: the relation type is recognised or explicitly recorded as unregistered
the capture is attributable to a named observing agent
effects: stores evidence only; an assertion is created solely by a separate authority-backed proposal
records that transport-level signals alone do not establish subject identity

functions.name: Register an external endpoint change and raise re-evaluation
functions.description: Ingest an externally decided merge, split, withdrawal, deactivation or reinstatement of an endpoint, mark every assertion naming that endpoint for re-evaluation and set interim admissibility. The endpoint decision and any master-data merge remain external.
inputs: reference to the deciding authority's change record and its effective instant
outputs: re-evaluation request with state and impacted assertion set
interim admissibility per impacted assertion
continuity hints for predecessor and successor endpoints
preconditions: the change is evidenced by the endpoint's own authority
the effective instant and ingestion instant are recorded separately
effects: opens a re-evaluation request without altering any endpoint or master record
retains all affected assertions rather than deleting them

functions.name: Emit change impact and readiness content
functions.description: Produce the impact and migration readiness report and the change notice content for a registered endpoint change over a stated interval, enumerating created, updated and deleted alias entries. Delivery, subscription and receipting are external.
inputs: interval start and optional end instants
outputs: change impact and migration readiness report
alias change notice content with per-entry change type
readiness signal
preconditions: the re-evaluation request has reached a reportable state
interval boundaries are expressed with seconds and explicit offset
effects: publishes report and notice content for consumers to collect
does not transmit, retry or acknowledge notifications

functions.name: Admit a contended proposal
functions.description: Accept or reject a proposed assertion change under an expected-version precondition, an idempotency key and a request fingerprint, replaying the original outcome for a recognised retry and recording duplicates and in-flight collisions explicitly.
outputs: concurrency outcome code
replayed original outcome for a recognised retry
duplicate-of reference where the proposal restates an existing assertion
preconditions: the normalised endpoint pair key can be computed
the key retention window is declared and current
effects: applies at most one state transition per idempotency key and fingerprint pair
rejects a mismatched precondition instead of overwriting
rejects reuse of a key with a different fingerprint

functions.name: Contain a disputed or harmful assertion
functions.description: Place an assertion into a contested, suppressed or quarantined state with a stated reason, expiry and tombstone statement, link any compensating action, and keep every prior decision and evidence item intact.
inputs: containment action code and stated reason
raising agent, instant and evidence threshold met
outputs: containment and compensation record with tombstone statement
updated per-member containment state
expiry instant and review obligation
preconditions: the raising agent holds the declared entitlement for the action
the assertion and its evidence are already durably retained
effects: suppresses the assertion from candidate sets while leaving it discoverable in diagnostics
never deletes an assertion, its evidence or an answer that cited it
enforcement of consumer visibility tiers is delegated to the adopting Dimension's access-control model

functions.name: Replay a previously issued answer
functions.description: Recompute a prior answer from this model's own retained inputs and compare the result with the stored answer record, to demonstrate that historical answering is deterministic.
inputs: its recorded as-of frame, pin manifest and determinant digest
outputs: replay verdict (reproduced, diverged, inputs unavailable)
divergence report naming the changed inputs
preconditions: the determinant input set and the pin manifest are still retained
the observation cut-off can be reapplied to the retained assertion population
effects: produces a verdict about this model's own records only
does not constitute or replace the consuming systems' audit trail, which is owned elsewhere

composition.purpose: Identifier syntax, namespace governance, authority delegation and persistence guarantees are defined by the parent; this mixin consumes governed identifiers as endpoints and adds equivalence assertion and resolution semantics only.

composition.target: Host entity, agent, place or product models needing federated identity equivalence
composition.purpose: Attach alias endpoints, assertion sets and as-of resolution behaviour to any host subject without duplicating its own identity or lifecycle model.

composition.target: Relation reasoning and equivalence inference model
composition.purpose: Carry the assertion, its authority and its confidence; delegate transitive, symmetric and reflexive closure, cluster formation and any entailment over equivalence to the reasoning model. OWL 2 places the formal consequences of SameIndividual in separate semantics documents, confirming the split.

composition.target: HTTP transport and dereference execution component
composition.purpose: Reference observed relocation and hint responses as evidence while leaving request execution, redirect following, connection handling and endpoint availability entirely to the transport component.
Declare visibility tiers and suppression fields on answers and containment records; evaluation and enforcement of any access decision remain with the authorization model.

composition.target: Master-data merge, survivorship and reconciliation model
composition.purpose: Consume an externally decided merge or split as a change event that triggers re-evaluation of local assertions; record merging, survivorship rules and golden-record construction stay external.
Hand prepared change notice and readiness content to the delivery model, which owns transport, subscription management, retry and receipting.

composition.target: Consumer audit trail and event log model
composition.purpose: Point answers and containment records at downstream audit systems for evidentiary use; this model retains its own decision records but owns no audit-trail semantics for how answers were consumed.
Align as-of resolution and version pinning with datetime negotiation, TimeGate and TimeMap where an endpoint authority offers them; alignment only, no conformance claimed.
Draw recognised hint relation types from the registry rather than minting local vocabulary, and record unregistered types explicitly as such.
Express assertion, observation, answer and containment provenance using Entity, Activity, Agent, wasGeneratedBy, wasAttributedTo, wasRevisionOf and generatedAtTime; alignment only.
Shape impact enumeration and change notice content as change lists with created, updated and deleted entries bounded by from and until instants.

composition.target: W3C DID Resolution v1 resolution metadata
composition.purpose: Align the closed resolution status vocabulary, versionTime and versionId options, and deactivated/canonicalId/equivalentId metadata with an existing resolver contract; the target specification is a Candidate Recommendation Draft, so alignment is provisional.

owner_package_requirements: The adopting Dimension names an accountable steward for the alias assertion population and a separate accountable owner for the resolution service that issues answers.
The Dimension declares, per endpoint namespace, which version-pin mechanism applies and which authority publishes endpoint condition and change events.
The Dimension publishes its hop budget, staleness budget, idempotency key retention window and quarantine expiry defaults as governed configuration with effective instants.
The Dimension states which retention and disposition policy governs tombstoned assertions and which authorization model enforces the declared visibility tiers.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Endpoint identifiers keep the namespace of their issuing authority and are never rewritten locally; this model's own records (assertions, answers, traces, evidence items, reports, containment records) live in a Dimension-owned namespace distinct from every endpoint namespace, so that a local record identifier can never be mistaken for an endpoint identifier or vice versa.
registry_links: IANA Link Relation Types registry for recognised hint relation types
Endpoint authority registries that publish status and continuity relationships, such as the Research Organization Registry status and predecessor/successor model
DOI registration agency metadata states distinguishing discoverable from registered-but-tombstoned identifiers

canonicalization_rules: All instants are canonicalised to RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset; an unknown local offset is preserved as -00:00 and is never normalised to Z.

The endpoint pair key is canonicalised as an ordered tuple of (source endpoint, direction, target endpoint, asserting authority) after each identifier is normalised by the rules its own authority publishes, with no local case folding or path rewriting.
Candidate sets in an answer are canonically ordered by a declared stable key so that the determinant digest is reproducible; ordering conveys no preference.
Hop traces are canonicalised as an ordered list preserving observation order, with duplicate endpoints retained rather than collapsed so cycles remain visible.
patch_rules: Assertions and answers are append-only: a correction creates a new record that references the prior one as its revision antecedent; the prior record is never edited in place.
A patch to a containment state must carry the raising agent, the reason and the expected-version token; a patch without a matching precondition is rejected rather than merged.
Evidence items and chain traces are immutable once captured; a later re-observation is a new item, never an update.
Patches that would remove an endpoint from an assertion are expressed as withdrawal plus a new assertion, so the historical answer for any past instant stays reproducible.
compatibility_rules: Resolution status codes may be added but never removed or redefined; a consumer encountering an unknown status treats it as a non-success and does not guess.
Adding a new pin mechanism or hint relation type is backward compatible; changing the meaning of an existing one requires a new code.
Reducing the hop budget or the staleness budget is a breaking change for reproducibility of current-mode answers and requires an effective instant and a change notice.
Historical answers issued under a prior rule set remain valid and are re-derivable only with the rule set version recorded on them; rule-set version is a required field on every answer.

identity_priority: The authoritative master-system identifier assigned by the system of record for the artifact's subject (the resolution service's answer register, the observing system's capture register, or the steward's decision register) takes precedence over all other identifiers.
A governed global identifier or IRI under the adopting Dimension's namespace, used only where no authoritative master-system identifier exists.
A UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension, used only where neither a master-system identifier nor a governed IRI is available.
A date, an interval boundary, a series ordinal or an endpoint pair key is never an identifier; each may only be an attribute of a record.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All time values are recorded in RFC 3339 form with seconds present and an explicit UTC offset or Z; an offset of -00:00 is retained to mean the local offset is unknown and is not silently replaced by Z. Event time (when the asserted equivalence, endpoint change or relocation took effect in the world) and observation or ingestion time (when this model captured or recorded it) are stored as separate fields on every assertion, evidence item, trace, change event and answer, and both are supplied on every as-of request; where they coincide, both are still written explicitly rather than inferred.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Records issued in a series (answer records, chain traces, impact reports, change notices, containment records) carry a monotonically increasing ordinal within a declared series scope together with the series identifier. The ordinal is an attribute used only for ordering and gap detection; the record's identity is always resolved by the identity priority above, and gaps or re-issues are recorded explicitly rather than by renumbering.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Every artifact carries a cryptographic digest over its canonical content; answers additionally carry a digest over their ordered determinant input set and a reference to the pin manifest, so that a replay can prove the same inputs yield the same answer. A digest mismatch marks the artifact as unverifiable and removes it from evidence eligibility without deleting it.

policies: No canonical endpoint is ever elected silently: an answer with more than one admissible endpoint returns the full candidate set with an ambiguity status, and an answer with none returns an explicit no-answer status with a reason.

No chain is followed without a bound: traversal of an observed hop sequence stops at the declared hop budget or on cycle detection, and the partial trace is retained as evidence with a termination reason.

A transport-level relocation, a canonical link or a published also-known-as statement is evidence only; an equivalence assertion exists only when a named authority stands behind it, and independent confirmation or reciprocity is recorded.

Nothing is erased to resolve a dispute: contested, superseded, withdrawn and quarantined assertions are retained with their evidence, and a tombstone statement replaces the suppressed content rather than an empty result.

Every state transition of an assertion is guarded by an expected-version precondition, and every externally initiated proposal is retry-safe through an idempotency key paired with a request fingerprint.

read: Reads are performed through as-of resolution with both an event instant and an observation cut-off; a read that omits them is treated as a current-mode read and is labelled as such on the answer.
A read never mutates assertion state; issuing an answer record is a separate, explicitly provenanced write.
Suppressed and quarantined assertions are absent from candidate sets but visible in a diagnostics section of the answer to entitled readers, so their absence is never silent.
Reads of historical answers return the stored answer record together with its rule-set version, pin manifest and determinant digest.
create: An assertion is created only by an authority-backed proposal that names the asserting authority, both endpoints, a validity start instant and at least one evidence reference.
Creation requires an idempotency key and request fingerprint where the proposer is an automated client, so that a retry replays the original outcome instead of creating a second assertion.
Captured hint evidence, chain traces and endpoint condition observations are created independently of assertions and never imply one.
Answer, impact report, change notice and containment records are created append-only with a series ordinal and full provenance.
update: Assertion content is never updated in place; a correction is a new revision record referencing its antecedent, and the antecedent remains resolvable.
Containment state and re-evaluation request state may transition, always under an expected-version precondition and always with the acting agent, reason and instant recorded.
Evidence items, chain traces and issued answers are immutable; a changed observation is a new capture with its own observation instant.
An update that would change a past answer is forbidden; late-arriving evidence produces a new answer for the same as-of instant, marked as a revision of the earlier one.
delete: This model performs no destructive delete of its own records. Withdrawal, supersession and quarantine set a state and publish a tombstone statement that names the record identifier, the prior claim and the reason it no longer applies, while the record and its evidence remain retained and resolvable, following registry practice that a registered identifier cannot be deleted and continues to resolve to a tombstone.

Retention periods for assertions, evidence items, chain traces, answers and containment records are set by the adopting Dimension's retention and disposition policy, which also owns and executes any eventual physical destruction; this model records the applicable retention class and the disposition due instant but never carries out disposition itself.

Where a legal erasure obligation applies to personal data inside an evidence item, the obligation and its execution belong to the adopting Dimension's privacy and retention model; this model supports it only by supporting redaction-in-place that preserves the record identifier, the digest of what was removed and the tombstone statement, so that historical answers remain explainable.

Endpoint deletion is out of scope entirely: an endpoint that disappears is recorded as a missing, unresolved or tombstoned condition observation, and deletion of the endpoint itself is owned by the endpoint's own authority.

roles.name: Alias steward
responsibilities: Adjudicate conflicting active assertions and close cluster re-evaluation requests
Approve promotion of captured hints into authority-backed proposals
Record the reason and evidence threshold for every containment action

roles.name: Resolution service owner
responsibilities: Operate deterministic as-of answering and publish the hop, staleness and rule-set versions in force
Guarantee that answers are immutable, digested and replayable
Ensure ambiguity and no-answer outcomes are emitted rather than suppressed

roles.name: Endpoint authority liaison
responsibilities: Register externally decided endpoint merge, split, withdrawal and reinstatement events with their effective and ingestion instants
Maintain the per-namespace version-pin mechanism declarations
Escalate endpoints whose condition cannot be observed within the staleness budget

roles.name: Evidence custodian
responsibilities: Capture hint evidence, chain traces and endpoint condition observations with attributable provenance
Verify artifact digests and mark unverifiable evidence as ineligible without deleting it
Preserve partial and looping traces as diagnostic evidence

roles.name: Change impact coordinator
responsibilities: Enumerate impacted assertions, answers and downstream references for each registered change event
Produce impact and migration readiness reports and change notice content
Hand notice content to the delivery model and track readiness signals

access.default_rule: Read access to alias assertions, answers and their provenance is granted to consumers entitled by the adopting Dimension; write access (proposal, revision, containment) is restricted to named authority-backed proposers and stewards. This model declares the entitlement fields and visibility tiers only; every access decision is evaluated and enforced by the adopting Dimension's authorization model.
exceptions: Quarantined and suppressed assertions are withheld from candidate sets for all consumers but remain visible in the diagnostics section to stewards and the evidence custodian, so their suppression is disclosed rather than hidden.

Evidence items containing personal or commercially sensitive captured representations may be restricted to the evidence custodian while their existence, digest and provenance stay visible to entitled readers.
Emergency quarantine may be raised by a single entitled role without prior review, subject to a mandatory expiry and a recorded review obligation.
Historical answers already issued to a consumer remain readable by that consumer even if the underlying assertion is later suppressed, because the answer records what was true at issue time.
audit_requirements: Every containment action, quarantine, compensating action and re-evaluation closure records the acting agent, the activity, the reason and both event and recording instants.
Every issued answer records its determinant input digest and rule-set version so that a replay can independently confirm determinism.
Records of access decisions and downstream consumption are written to the adopting Dimension's audit-trail model; this model produces the evidence to be audited but owns no audit-trail semantics.

required_fields: Owner or maintainer designated by the adopting Dimension
Rule-set version in force with its effective instant
Declared hop budget, staleness budget, idempotency key retention window and quarantine expiry defaults
read_order: AGENTS.md for the bootstrap contract, owner and the currently effective rule-set version
Specification URL for the model boundary, scope exclusions and the closed resolution status vocabulary
Storage type URL for how assertions, evidence, traces and answers are persisted in this deployment
Interface URL for how as-of resolution and proposal admission are invoked in this deployment
Processes URL for re-evaluation, containment, impact reporting and replay procedures

coverage.claim: This model gives a defensible, source-grounded structure for historical (as-of) alias resolution and the operational edge cases around it: dual-timeline as-of framing, endpoint version pinning, a closed and deterministic outcome vocabulary including ambiguity and no-answer, endpoint condition tracking, bounded chain traversal with loop detection and relocation classification, hints treated as evidence rather than identity proof, merge/split impact and readiness reporting, and contention, duplication, compensation and quarantine controls. It does not claim completeness over identifier governance, equivalence inference, transport execution, authorization or master-data merge, each of which is bounded out with a cited neighbour.

checklist.notes: Identity priority puts the authoritative master-system identifier first, then a governed IRI, then a Dimension-assigned UUID or ULID; series ordinals, endpoint pair keys and dates are explicitly barred from being identifiers. Endpoint identifiers remain governed by their issuing authority and by the parent model.

Assertion states (proposed, active, contested, suppressed, quarantined, superseded, withdrawn, reinstated), quarantine expiry and escalation, and re-evaluation request states are specified. Grounded in registry practice where identifiers move to inactive or withdrawn rather than being deleted.

Predecessor and successor continuity hints, duplicate-of references, revision antecedents and conflict-set membership are modelled. Inference and closure over equivalence relations are delegated to a relation-reasoning model, per the OWL 2 split between assertion and semantics.

Event/validity time and observation/ingestion time are separate mandatory fields; as-of requests carry both; RFC 3339 with seconds and explicit offset is enforced, and -00:00 is preserved as unknown local offset. Memento supplies the as-of access pattern.
Every assertion, evidence item, trace, answer and containment action carries agent, activity, generation instant and revision antecedent, aligned to PROV-O terms.
Five roles with distinct responsibilities; deciding authority for endpoint changes, accountable steward for re-evaluation and named consumers for readiness reports are all recorded as data.

Pin verification, reciprocity and authority checks before hint promotion, digest verification, determinant-digest replay, non-determinism conditions that forbid emitting an answer, and semantic duplicate detection.

Visibility tiers, disclosed suppression rather than silent absence, and four exceptions are declared; evaluation and enforcement are explicitly delegated to the adopting Dimension's authorization model. Registry practice of a registered-but-not-discoverable state supports gating visibility without erasure.

No destructive delete of this model's records; withdrawal produces a tombstone stating identifier, prior claim and reason while the record stays resolvable. Retention classes and disposition due instants are recorded here; disposition execution and any legal erasure obligation belong to the adopting Dimension's retention and privacy policy.
Alignments to Memento, the IANA link relations registry, PROV-O, ResourceSync change documents and DID Resolution metadata, all recorded as alignments with no conformance claimed.
Canonical candidate ordering, determinant input digest, rule-set version on every answer and an explicit replay function with a divergence verdict.

Optimistic preconditions and precondition-failure rejection rest on a full IETF standard, but the idempotency key plus fingerprint pattern rests on an expired Internet-Draft rather than a published standard. The structure is retained because the failure mode is real, and the node is marked as lacking settled normative support.

RFC 9110 only advises that clients SHOULD detect cyclical redirections and merely notes a historical five-redirect recommendation. There is no normative maximum hop count, so the declared budget is a local governance decision presented as such rather than as a standards requirement.

Confidence values are carried through answers unchanged, but no authoritative source was found that fixes a comparable scale, calibration method or aggregation rule for cross-authority equivalence confidence. Quantification is deliberately left undefined rather than invented.

Artifact digests, idempotency key scoping and expiry, rejection of key reuse with a differing fingerprint, and entitlement-gated containment actions. Authentication and authorization mechanisms themselves are out of boundary.
Alias resolution is not spatially indexed. Where an aliased subject is a place, spatial identity belongs to the host entity model and to the endpoint authority, not to this mixin.

known_omissions: No cost or performance model for re-observation, so the staleness budget is declared without guidance on how to size it.
Bulk or set-wise as-of resolution over large identifier populations is not modelled; only single-subject resolution semantics are specified.

Cryptographic countersignature of assertions by both endpoint authorities is not modelled, although reciprocity is recorded; verifiable attestation would strengthen promotion but no settled cross-authority mechanism was identified.

Partial or scoped equivalence (same subject in one context, distinct in another) is acknowledged only through direction and asserting authority; contextual scoping of equivalence is not developed here.
No guidance is given on reconciling an endpoint authority whose own as-of answers change retroactively without notice.
conflicts: RFC 6596 defines canonical as a preference over duplicative or superset content and RFC 8288 warns against inferring extra semantics from relation types, yet common practice treats a canonical link as an identity statement. This model follows the specifications and treats it as evidence only, which will disagree with tools that equate the two.

DID Core advises against treating an alsoKnownAs relation as equivalence unless it is reciprocated, while much published linked data asserts one-directional same-as without reciprocity. This model records the asymmetry rather than resolving it.

Memento leaves best-match selection to server discretion, so two authorities can return different states for the same requested datetime; this model pins and records what it received rather than asserting a single correct historical state.

ROR does not require predecessor and successor relationships to be bidirectional, so a merge or split may be discoverable from only one side; enumeration of impacted references can therefore be incomplete through no fault of this model.
The DID Resolution alignment is to a Candidate Recommendation Draft whose dereferencing section is marked at risk, so status-vocabulary alignment may need revision.
RFC 3339 permits leap seconds while several storage and query stacks reject or smear them; the canonicalisation rule preserves what was received and the divergence is recorded rather than hidden.
regional_assumptions: Timestamps are assumed to be recorded with an explicit UTC offset regardless of jurisdiction; deployments relying on local civil time without an offset must convert before ingestion and record -00:00 where the original offset is genuinely unknown.

Legal erasure obligations differ by jurisdiction; the model assumes the adopting Dimension holds a policy that names which obligation applies and executes it, and it makes no assumption that erasure is or is not required.

Identifier authorities cited here are internationally scoped research and web registries; national identifier registers may forbid retaining a withdrawn identifier at all, which would conflict with the retain-and-tombstone default and requires a Dimension-level exception.

Evidence capture of published representations may be constrained by copyright or database rights that vary by jurisdiction; the model assumes digests and provenance may always be retained even where the payload cannot.
adversarial_checks: Does any bundle, layer, finding or function claim ownership of redirect execution, endpoint availability, authorization evaluation, data merge or equivalence inference? Checked: chain handling ingests observed hops and never dereferences; endpoint condition is an observation pointing at the endpoint authority; access declares fields and delegates enforcement; endpoint change is registered, not decided; inference is delegated with an explicit composition link.

Could an answer be produced that silently picks one endpoint or follows an unbounded chain? Checked: ambiguity returns the full candidate set with an ambiguity status, an exhausted budget and a detected loop each produce their own status with the partial trace retained, and non-determinism conditions forbid emitting an answer at all.

Could a past answer change without trace? Checked: append-only assertions and immutable answers, dual timelines with an observation cut-off, rule-set version and determinant digest on every answer, and a replay function that reports divergence rather than overwriting.

Does any structural node rest only on secondary sources or on assumption? Checked: every node cites at least one primary source; the two nodes whose normative support is weak (hop budget, idempotency keys) are marked as gaps rather than presented as canonical, and confidence quantification is left undefined rather than fabricated.

Does the model duplicate the parent identifier model or a sibling? Checked: no identifier minting, syntax, persistence guarantee or authority-delegation content is modelled here; each is bounded out with a cited neighbour note and a composition link.

Does containment or quarantine amount to an audit-trail or enforcement claim? Checked: containment sets state and publishes a tombstone on this model's own records; enforcement of visibility and the audit trail of consumption are both delegated outward with explicit composition links.
